target: Route "rlt-two": The level-two choice lift — the merged matrix M(G), rl:merge / rl:levels / rl:splitters / rl:cone / rl:modulator / rl:tree-vacuous
verdict:
Four of the five results survive; one (rl:modulator) is broken, and two others are theorems about an undefined object. I rebuilt every computation independently in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/296b18c1-9dc5-4a0b-94cf-9bde3946ecfe/scratchpad/r18-audit-rlt-two-correctness (own game builder, own exact first-passage rows, own Balas extended formulation for R_1, own block system for R_j, own merged matrix / transience / CR_j, own escape-certificate solver; w* by LP least-element and cross-checked against brute force over all positional strategies wherever |C| <= 7).

WHAT REPRODUCED, EXACTLY. (i) rl:merge-bound, rl:merge, rl:splitters, rl:cone: I reconstructed all four proofs step by step and they are correct given a definition of R_j; I also checked D <= MD numerically on three explicit R_1 points (the tree certificates at d = 1,2,3). (ii) W_14: normal form, Q box ([1/2,1],[1/2,1],[15/32,1]), R_1 box ([1/2,3/5],[1/2,23/40],[15/32,11/20]), R_2 = {w*}, mu = 1, sp = 1 — all exactly as claimed, with two independent implementations of level one agreeing. (iii) D1: built as a genuine 14-vertex out-degree-two stopping SSG from the stated rows; w* = 1/4 everywhere, M non-transient, no single freezing works (mu_rl = 2), CR_2(D1) = {0}, R_2(D1) = {w*} — rl:cone's strictness claim confirmed. (iv) rl:tree-vacuous: the certificate (x, A, w*, every Y^u, Z^u, every pin, every convex identity, membership in Q entrywise) verified in exact rational arithmetic FROM THE BUILT GAME for twelve parameter triples, three of them freshly generated and not in the route's list; the matching exact upper bounds max_{R_1} x(root) = 2/3, 4/5, 4/7, 6/11 recomputed at T_1(3,1/2), T_2(3,1/2), T_2(3,1/4), T_1(2,3/8). (v) Escape certificates: lambda_d = (8d+22)/(8d+23) and kappa(x_d) = (8d+23)/2 recomputed exactly for d = 1..5, consistent with the proved bound 1-lambda >= 1/(9d+28). (vi) Table: fourteen rows recomputed (G8, S, S_r(3), H_3, H_4, H_5, L_2..L_6, W_14, W_10, the 7-vertex rem:own-stall game, WD(4,2,6), WD(6,3,7), CC(1,2), CC(2,2)) — every mu and every first exact level matches. (vii) sp(T_d) = mu(T_d) = 2^d - 1 at d = 1,2; CR_2(T_1) = {0}, CR_2(T_2) != {0}; level two exact at the root of T_1, T_2, T_3 (float), consistent with "no level-two gap found".

WHAT BROKE. rl:modulator is refuted on the route's own instances: thm:modulator freezes by RETYPING a vertex as a terminal with arbitrary payoff (row and column both leave M, so the condition is transience of the principal submatrix M_BB), while rl:levels freezes by COMMITTING a controlled vertex to one action (transience of M^{A,p} for every p). Only one direction holds. Measured mu_rl vs thm:modulator's number: (2,1) on WD(4,2,6), WD(6,3,7), CC(1,2), CC(2,2), D1; (3,1) on T_2(3,1/4). So "first exact level <= 1 + mu_M(G)" is unproved and the headline "the first exact level, wherever it can be bounded at all, is thm:modulator's number in disguise" is false. Separately, rl:levels and rl:cone quantify over R_j for j >= 2 — an object neither frontier.tex nor the route's LaTeX defines; the proof runs on notation (z^{S,T}, X^{S,T}, F_A^p, "clauses of the level-j definition") that exists only in the route's sa.py. And rl:where imports rem:choice-lift's rho_max clause as an established constraint when rem:choice-lift explicitly records it as unproved.

NET. rl:merge, rl:levels, rl:splitters, rl:cone and rl:tree-vacuous stand as mathematics (the middle two conditionally on writing the R_j definition into the paper). rl:modulator does not, and with it the "modulator number in disguise" half of the headline. sound = false.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP (all clean): no greedy policy iteration anywhere (least fixed points / LPs, cross-checked by brute force over all strategies); constraint rows accumulated with += rather than dict literals; sinks carried as sentinels n, n+1; traps computed over non-sinks only; every vertex of T_d is reachable from the root, so the class memberships are properties of the instance as posed; the witnesses are dyadic and every value is verified from the built game rather than from a normal form; the claimed easy classes (thm:few-avg, thm:escape-class, thm:one-player) are correctly named, and the route states outright that no new polynomial class can come from a one-player exactness theorem; the route claims no decision-rule stall, so the three readings of the standing rule do not bite. NOT CHECKED: the CV, BC, R, G*, DW rows of the table; the 303,750-system enumeration; d = 6,7 certificates; D2, D3 and the "uniform-mixing families", which are defined nowhere.

findings.result_name: rl:modulator — the certifiable level is a freezing-modulator number
findings.defect: The identification "the hypothesis of rl:levels at A says precisely that A is a freezing modulator of G into M in the sense of thm:modulator" is FALSE in the direction the route needs, so the displayed inequality (first exact level) <= 1 + mu_M(G) does not follow and the headline claim that the first exact level is thm:modulator's number in disguise is refuted. thm:modulator's freezing is retyping a non-terminal as a TERMINAL with arbitrary payoff, which deletes both the row and the column of that vertex from the merged matrix, so the condition is transience of the principal submatrix M_BB with B = C minus A, independent of theta. rl:levels' freezing commits a controlled vertex to one ACTION and asks transience of M^{A,p} for every p, which is strictly stronger: M_BB is a principal submatrix of M^{A,p}, so the route's hypothesis implies the modulator condition but not conversely. The valid statement is level <= 1 + mu_rl with the route's own number, which can strictly exceed thm:modulator's.
findings.evidence: Computed exactly (merge.py: mu_rl = least |A| with M^{A,p} transient for all p; mu_modulator = least |A| with M_BB transient; transience decided by the least nonnegative solution of y = My + 1). D1 (the route's own example, built as a 14-vertex stopping SSG): mu_rl = 2, thm:modulator's number = 1 — freezing v_1 to a terminal leaves M_BB on (v_2,a,b) whose only cycle v_2 -> a -> v_2 has weight 7/8, rho = sqrt(7/8) < 1; whereas committing v_1 to action 0 leaves the 2x2 block [[0,7/8],[7/8,7/8]] of the square, eigenvalue (7/8)(1+sqrt5)/2 = 1.4158 > 1. Same split on WD(4,2,6) (2 vs 1), WD(6,3,7) (2 vs 1), CC(1,2) (2 vs 1), CC(2,2) (2 vs 1), and worst on T_2(3,1/4): mu_rl = 3 while deleting the root alone makes M transient, so thm:modulator's number is 1 and the route's bound gives level <= 4 where the modulator number would give 2. The JSON verification field for this result asserts "on every instance where rl:levels certifies exactness at level mu+1 ... thm:modulator's exponent is mu", which these six instances contradict.

findings.result_name: rl:levels and rl:splitters — a freezing set, and incomparable rows, bound the exact level
findings.defect: rl:levels and rl:cone are theorems about R_j for j >= 2, an object defined NOWHERE — not in frontier.tex (rem:choice-lift gives only level zero and the level-one Balas description, then says "the level-j Sherali-Adams lift") and not in the route's paste-ready LaTeX (rl:notation defers to rem:choice-lift). The proof of rl:levels then runs on undefined notation: "level-j family (z^{S,T}, X^{S,T})", "F_A^p", "satisfies every clause of the level-(j-|A|) definition". The statements have no truth value as written: the load-bearing step — that pinning any j-1 coordinates decomposes x into R_1 pieces — is a property of one particular formalisation, not a consequence of the phrase "Sherali-Adams lift". The proof additionally needs the homogenised box row U[p] <= z[p]*1 (to force P_p = 0 when lambda_p = 0, the case the proof waves through with "whenever lambda_p > 0"), and that row exists only in the route's sa.py.
findings.evidence: grep of frontier.tex for choice-lift returns exactly two hits, l.14981 (rem:choice-lift) and l.17954 (the summary); rem:choice-lift defines R_0 = Q(G) and R_1 = cap_v conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1) and nothing else. rl.tex l.5-17 (rl:notation) repeats only those two. The working definition sits in the route's sa.py docstring (blocks p in {None,0,1}^m, variables z[p], U[p], clauses (i)-(iv)); I reimplemented it independently in lift.py:Rj_system and it reproduces the route's numbers (R_1 box of W_14 identical to my Balas extended formulation, R_2(W_14) = {w*} coordinatewise), so the theorem is true FOR THAT DEFINITION — which is not in the paper and not in the paste-ready text.

findings.result_name: rl:where — where a level-two gap can live
findings.defect: An explicitly unproved claim of frontier.tex is cited as an established constraint. rl:where says "by \Cref{rem:choice-lift} it has at least three Max vertices and at least three of them reversing", and the JSON gap field repeats it. But rem:choice-lift says of exactly that clause: "What the route reported the hierarchy to give --- max_{R_j} x = w* once j >= min(|Vmax|, rho_max+1) ... --- it did not prove, and it is recorded here as a claim." The "at least three of them reversing" half rests on nothing else, and it shaped the search reported in the same remark.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.14981 ff., final sentences of rem:choice-lift, verbatim: "it did not prove, and it is recorded here as a claim". The other half of the imported constraint, |Vmax| >= 3, is independently true for a reason the route does not give: R_{|C|}(G) = {w*} on every stopping game, because a block pinning every controlled vertex forces Tx = x on a game with a unique fixed point, so a level-two gap needs |C| >= 3 with no appeal to rho_max.

findings.result_name: rl:tree-vacuous — level one is asymptotically vacuous, on a one-player family with five average vertices
findings.defect: The minimality claim in rl:tree-threshold, "The smallest instance is T_2(3,1/4): 14 vertices", is false: two smaller members of the same family straddle the threshold.
findings.evidence: Built from rl:tree-def and verified entrywise in exact rational arithmetic from the built game (cert.py) and by exact LP over the Balas extended formulation (lift.py:box_R1): T_1(2,3/8) has N = 10, |C| = 3, a = 5, w*(root) = 3/8 and exact R_1 root interval [3/8, 6/11], with 3/8 < 1/2 < 6/11; T_2(2,1/4) has N = 13, a = 4 and exact R_1 root interval [1/4, 4/7]. Both satisfy the theorem's hypotheses (2(3/4 - 3/8) = 3/4 >= 5/8 and 4(3/4 - 1/4) = 2 >= 3/4). The substantive comparison with rem:choice-lift's 27-vertex DW survives a fortiori; only the word "smallest" fails.

findings.result_name: rl:tree-vacuous — level one is asymptotically vacuous, on a one-player family with five average vertices
findings.defect: rl:tree-threshold drops a hypothesis of the theorem it invokes: it assumes only kappa < 1/2 and 2^d > (1-kappa)/kappa, then says "the upper bound is \Cref{rl:tree-vacuous}", but rl:tree-vacuous also requires 2^d(g-kappa) >= 1-kappa, which does not follow.
findings.evidence: kappa = 7/16, e = 1 (so g = 1/2), d = 1: kappa < 1/2 and 2 > (1-kappa)/kappa = 9/7, so the corollary's hypotheses hold, while 2(g-kappa) = 1/8 < 9/16 = 1-kappa, so the theorem's do not and its vector x is not shown to lie in Q. The named instance T_2(3,1/4) does satisfy the missing hypothesis (4(7/8-1/4) = 5/2 >= 3/4), so the corollary's own example is safe; the general statement is not proved as written.

findings.result_name: rl:merge — the merged matrix bounds the level-one relaxation
findings.defect: The why_not_implied asserts "the ladder L_n has every vertex reversing and a nilpotent M, so rl:merge decides it and the reversing count says nothing". The ladder has ZERO reversing vertices, so rem:choice-lift's reversing count decides it at level one, and in fact Q(L_n) is already the single point w*, so it is decided at level zero. The incomparability the route wants is nevertheless true, with a witness the route does not name.
findings.evidence: Computed exactly (rho.py: the number of Max vertices whose successor difference x(v^(0)) - x(v^(1)) takes both signs on Q(G)): rho_max(L_3) = rho_max(L_4) = 0, and box_Q(L_n) = {w*} coordinatewise for n = 2..6 (first exact level 0), because x(v_n) >= x(t_1) = 1 pins the whole ladder at 1. The correct witness for "rl:levels sharper than the reversing count" is W_14: rho_max = 3, so min(|Vmax|, rho+1) = 3 gives exactness only at level three, while mu_rl = 1 gives level two, which is the true first exact level.

findings.result_name: rl:modulator — the certifiable level is a freezing-modulator number
findings.defect: Wrong citation: "Freezing c in C to its action i (\Cref{def:freeze})". def:freeze is the freezing SWITCHING RULE rho_B for a set B of AVERAGE vertices, which declares the average vertices outside B terminals with payoff val_sigma and re-optimises Max — a different object from committing a controlled vertex to one of its two actions.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.9901: "\begin{definition}[Freezing rule]\label{def:freeze} Let $B\subseteq\Vavg$. Given $\sigma$, put $x:=\val_\sigma$ and let $\widehat G_B(x)$ be the game played on $B\cup\Vmax\cup\Vmin$ ...". No notion of freezing a controlled vertex to an action is defined anywhere in frontier.tex; thm:modulator's freezing is retyping non-terminals as terminals.

findings.result_name: rl:levels and rl:splitters — a freezing set, and incomparable rows, bound the exact level
findings.defect: rl:levels is stated only for |A| = j-1 exactly, but rl:splitters applies it with A the set of splitters, whose size sp(G) is in general strictly less than j-1 (the corollary concludes for every j > sp(G)). The padding step — enlarging A preserves the hypothesis, because replacing a further row M_c by p^{c,i} <= M_c only decreases the matrix and transience is monotone in the entries — is used but not stated.
findings.evidence: rl.tex, statement of rl:levels ("let A subset C with |A| = j-1") against the proof of rl:splitters ("Take A to be the set of splitters in \Cref{rl:levels}"), with sp(W_14) = 1 < j-1 for every j >= 3 while the corollary asserts R_j = {w*} for all j > 1.

findings.result_name: rl:cone — the cone relaxation certifies exactness in one linear programme
findings.defect: Verification evidence rests on instances defined nowhere: "the five-vertex overlapping-router game D2", "the three-router cycle D3", "the uniform-mixing families with sp(G) = |C|", "the router trees with shared leaves". Only D1 is specified. Separately, the JSON reports the four-vertex search as "an exhaustive enumeration of the 50625 four-vertex one-player topologies", dropping the restriction the LaTeX does state — each action a constant or a gain-scaled read of ONE controlled vertex — under which it is exhaustive over a proper subfamily only (it excludes every action whose first-passage row spreads over two controlled vertices, which W_14's own rows do not but many games' do).
findings.evidence: rl.tex rl:cone and rl:where give explicit rows for D1 and none for D2 or D3, while the JSON verification fields of results 3 and 4 cite them as evidence. 15^4 = 50625 counts unordered action pairs drawn from {constant} u {read v : v in C} with |C| = 4, i.e. 5 options per action and C(6,2) = 15 per vertex — a subfamily, not all four-vertex one-player topologies.

findings.result_name: rl:levels and rl:splitters — a freezing set, and incomparable rows, bound the exact level
findings.defect: rl:splitters never beats a one-line fact when every vertex is a splitter: R_{|C|}(G) = {w*} on every stopping SSG (a block pinning all of C forces x(v) = x(v^(sigma(v))) together with x in Q, hence Tx = x, hence x = w* by uniqueness of the fixed point), so "exact for j > sp(G)" adds nothing once sp(G) = |C| — exactly the case for the "uniform-mixing families" the route cites.
findings.evidence: Measured: sp(WD(4,2,6)) = sp(CC(1,2)) = sp(CC(2,2)) = 2 = |C| (vacuous, the trivial bound already gives level 2); sp(D1) = 2 with |C| = 4 (informative); sp(T_1) = 1, sp(T_2) = 3 (informative).

findings.result_name: rl:levels and rl:splitters — a freezing set, and incomparable rows, bound the exact level
findings.defect: The proof of rl:levels does not say what P_p is when lambda_p = 0; it defines y_p only "whenever lambda_p > 0" and then sets P_p := lambda_p(y_p - w*). The gap closes only through the homogenised box row U[p] <= z[p]*1 of the (unwritten) definition of R_j, which forces U[p] = 0 there.
findings.evidence: rl.tex, proof of rl:levels, second paragraph; the corresponding row is clause (iii) "0 <= U <= z" in the route's sa.py, which the paste-ready text does not carry.

findings.result_name: rl:tree-vacuous — level one is asymptotically vacuous, on a one-player family with five average vertices
findings.defect: Under-claiming: rl:tree-remark reports max_{R_2} x(root) = w*(root) for T_1 "by exact dual certificates", but R_2(T_1) = {w*} is a theorem of the route itself (sp(T_1) = 1, so rl:splitters gives it), and rl:cone gives it too. Reporting a proved statement as measured understates the result.
findings.evidence: Measured sp(T_1(3,1/2)) = 1 (merge.py) and CR_2(T_1(3,1/2)) = {0} by exact LP; both are proofs, not measurements.

findings.result_name: rl:modulator — the certifiable level is a freezing-modulator number
findings.defect: Two vacuous comparisons in the surrounding prose. "thm:modulator already decides such a game in N^{O(mu_M)}, one power cheaper than the level-(mu_M+1) programme" compares two N^{O(.)} bounds on a class of ONE-PLAYER games, every member of which thm:one-player already decides in polynomial time (the route does say so). And the JSON's "transience of M gives an escape certificate (via the least solution of x = Sx+1)" is true of every stopping game, so it carries no information.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex thm:one-player (l.2176) computes val of any Vmin-empty SSG by one linear programme; lem:escape-rate (l.1775 ff.) gives lambda*(G) < 1 iff G is stopping, so the least solution of x = Sx + 1 is finite on every stopping game — which my escape.py confirms by returning a finite tau on every instance tried.
